comparisons.finding: A=7.8, F=7.0, overall=7.3. The substantial artifact preview and restrained brass rules suit the product. Download, video and invitation receive nearly equal emphasis; the remaining-reading counter distracts from sharing. At 200%, Download remains visible, but its supporting format information approaches the viewport edge. Passing production export and browser checks give this candidate the strongest implementation evidence. Video error handling is reported, but successful video is unverified. Artifact disclaimer text remains tiny at both text sizes.

A=8.7, F=5.4, weighted overall=6.7; delivered-task gate caps overall at 4.0 because prototype Download produces no file. Best proposed Share composition. The poster, explicit format and broad primary button form a clear sequence; privacy reassurance is immediately visible at normal size. Secondary tools stay subordinate. At 200%, the primary button remains visible, although reassurance continues below the initial viewport. The poetic heading is less direct than 'Share this glimpse,' and the smaller poster makes its embedded text harder to inspect. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: header [8,8,9,8,N/A,7]; poster/format [9,8,9,9,N/A,6]; download [9,9,9,9,0,8]; privacy copy [8,8,9,9,N/A,8]; secondary disclosure [8,8,8,7,N/A,7]. Feedback=0 represents the known missing download outcome, not an inferred visual state.

A=8.1, F=5.1, weighted overall=6.3; delivered-task gate caps overall at 4.0. Visible tool rows, privacy reassurance and video-unavailable copy make the options unusually explicit. However, the eyebrow, page heading and second editorial headline spend too much attention before the task. At 200%, the pairing becomes a long vertical sequence and pushes Download close to the viewport bottom. The thumbnail is too small to review the exported reading comfortably. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: header [8,8,9,8,N/A,7]; heading/eyebrow [7,8,8,7,N/A,7]; artifact/editorial pairing [7,7,9,7,N/A,5]; download [9,9,9,9,0,8]; privacy copy [8,8,9,9,N/A,8]; invitation/reminder rows [8,8,8,8,N/A,7]; video-unavailable notice [7,7,8,9,N/A,7]. The explicit unavailable notice is good state communication, but cannot compensate for the missing primary output.

A=8.6, F=5.2, weighted overall=6.6; delivered-task gate caps overall at 4.0. Best artifact presentation: a large preview, direct title and strong Download button preserve the mystical object as the focal point. At 200%, Download remains visible and the secondary strip appears to reflow vertically. The tradeoff is weaker informed sharing: privacy is hidden, and the visible invitation has less explanation about what it includes. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: header [8,8,9,8,N/A,7]; poster/format [9,8,9,9,N/A,7]; download [9,9,9,9,0,8]; invitation/reminder strip [8,8,8,7,N/A,7]; privacy/formats disclosure [7,8,8,7,N/A,7]. Strong gallery composition, but A gives more useful reassurance before the action.

A=6.6, F=6.2, overall=6.4. The orb and prediction establish emotional continuity, but consume most of an explanation screen. At 200%, the prediction breaks 'conversational' inside the word, introductory text is visibly clipped near the top, and the explanation falls below the initial viewport. This is substantial reading friction despite the supplied passing browser evidence. Below-fold evidence is not treated as missing. At 200%, text wraps cleanly, but the title, result and disclaimer delay the reasoning; reaching answers and assumptions requires substantial scrolling. The reasoning remains a dense paragraph. A=7.8, F=6.3, overall=6.9. The editorial treatment is coherent, but the section-navigation row competes with headings and provides ambiguous selected-state cues: all visible links have similar underlines. At 200%, the row extends beyond the visible content area and 'Assumptions' is cut off. The inset rule also reduces the reasoning's line width, increasing scrolling. The initial view lacks the result context provided by A and B; this is a context cost, not a claim that evidence was deleted. Component scores [hierarchy, typography, surfaces, clarity, feedback, accessibility]: header [8,8,9,8,N/A,7]; page title [8,8,9,8,N/A,8]; section navigation [6,5,8,6,6,4]; inset reasoning [8,7,9,8,N/A,6]; answer list [8,8,8,9,N/A,7]; assumptions section [8,8,8,8,N/A,7]. Working section links do not resolve the visible enlargement problem.

shareWinner: A — composition winner; baseline remains the implementation winner.
whyWinner: B — strongest balance of result context, explanation and discoverable evidence.
reason: Share A gives the clearest sequence from preview to Download to privacy reassurance, with secondary tools appropriately subordinate. C wins on preview size; B wins on immediately visible tool explanations. Why B makes the explanation primary while keeping answers, assumptions and the absence of sources legible as separate categories. A is the strongest alternative for uninterrupted reading. No candidate meets the authorized A>=9 and F>=9 threshold for every screen and component. The preferred compositions are design selections, not shipping approvals.
limitations: Independent assessment used only the four attached sheets and the supplied evidence boundaries. No source, history, prior grades or other graders were inspected.

Component tuples use [hierarchy, typography/spacing, surface/color coherence, task clarity, feedback/recovery, accessibility]. N/A is excluded from component means. Component scores are reported separately; screen scores assess the whole composition.
A is the mean of hierarchy, typography and surfaces; F is the mean of clarity, feedback and accessibility. Overall uses 0.4A+0.6F before rounding. Hard gates override averages.

Share prototype feedback=0 records the explicitly missing primary download result. Their gated overall scores assess present task completion; their hierarchy, clarity and accessibility scores describe provisional structural expectations. Placeholder outbound tools also require implementation.

Feedback scores elsewhere cover only visible state communication or explicitly supplied behavior. Screenshots cannot establish press, loading, error recovery, transition continuity, focus restoration or assistive announcements.

Alternatives require real export with verified file contents, truthful progress/success/failure states and retry, implemented secondary actions or explicit unavailable states, and verified disclosure/navigation semantics. Share C should expose essential privacy reassurance before export; Why C needs accessible navigation at 200%.
The fixed artwork's small embedded text does not enlarge with surrounding UI text. Export resolution labels do not prove preview readability or accessible equivalents.

Exact target sizes, measured prototype contrast, reduced-motion behavior, full scrolling, empty/loading/error states and real-device behavior were not verified. Viewport boundaries alone are not treated as deleted content or inaccessible controls.

Baseline browser evidence is credited as supplied, but does not erase screenshot-visible enlargement friction. Native and physical assistive-technology checks remain unverified; no 9/10 certification is made.
All candidates use the same reading. These judgments concern composition and interaction evidence, not predictive accuracy or model quality.
